description: Claim 1 is a dermatology visit with a skin biopsy. The plan denied the biopsy: its plan-approved amount, plan's share and member's share are all $0, and a denial note says why. The back page explains denials and how to appeal, and claim 2 (lab tests) is correct. Nothing here is an error: a careful reviewer should record the denial, note that the member owes nothing for the biopsy, and note the right to appeal.

note.text: Tessara Complete did not cover this biopsy because the medical records we received do not show it was medically necessary. You owe nothing for it. You can appeal this decision; the back page explains how.
note.rule: In-network service denied without advance notice: the member owes nothing (plan design, consistent with 42 CFR 422.504(g)(1)(i)); written notice with reasons and appeal rights under 42 CFR 422.568(d)-(e), https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/42/422.568

sources.what: If your plan denies coverage, it must tell you in writing, and you have the right to appeal
sources.source: Medicare.gov, Understanding Medicare Advantage Plans (CMS Product No. 12026), https://www.medicare.gov/publications/12026-understanding-medicare-advantage-plans.pdf

sources.what: A plan's written denial notice must give the specific reasons and explain the right to a reconsideration
sources.source: Cornell LII, 42 CFR 422.568 Standard timeframes and notice requirements for organization determinations, https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/42/422.568

sources.what: Contracted providers may not hold enrollees liable for fees that are the MA organization's obligation
Follow the plan's denial notice to appeal; the appeal must be filed within 65 days of that notice
sources.source: Medicare.gov, Appeals in Medicare health plans, https://www.medicare.gov/providers-services/claims-appeals-complaints/appeals/medicare-health-plans
